jsonld.site_description: Find every civic district that covers a point or address in Virginia, and who represents you there.
jsonld.app_description: Click any point in Virginia, or search an address, to see every civic district that contains it, and who represents you there — county or independent city, Virginia Senate, House of Delegates and U.S. House districts, magisterial districts, towns and cities, school divisions and ZIP codes.

head.title: Virginia district lookup — districtry Virginia
head.description: Tap the map or search a Virginia address: county or city, Virginia Senate, House of Delegates and U.S. House districts — and who represents you.

layers.label: U.S. House
layers.rank_note: 11 congressional districts — the largest districts Virginia carries below the state itself

source.answers: The U.S. House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 0 (120th Congressional Districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 11 features for Virginia, measured 2026-10-29. For Virginia it is the same map as layer 4 (119th Congressional Districts), district for district: the map the Supreme Court of Virginia adopted in December 2021, which stays in force for the 2026 election because that court struck down the 2026 redistricting amendment on 8 May 2026. The builder refuses to write if the two layers stop matching before 3 January 2027. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.

layers.label: Virginia Senate District
layers.rank_note: 40 Senate districts — larger on average than a county, smaller than a congressional district

source.answers: The Virginia Senate district covering the point, and the senator holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 1 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Upper), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 40 features for Virginia, measured 2026-10-29: the Senate districts the Supreme Court of Virginia adopted in December 2021, first used in 2023. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: va-senate-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the Senate of Virginia's own member list and each senator's page: the name, the party, the e-mail address, and the session office in the General Assembly Building with its telephone. A vacant seat carries a record saying so.

layers.rank_note: 100 House of Delegates districts — larger on average than a county or independent city, smaller than a Senate district

source.answers: The House of Delegates district covering the point, and the delegate holding it.

source.people: va-house-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the Virginia House of Delegates' own member list and each delegate's page: the name, the party, the e-mail address, and the Capitol office in the General Assembly Building with its telephone. The member list showed District 20 as vacant on 2026-10-29, and a vacant seat carries a record saying so.

layers.label: County or City
layers.rank_note: 133 counties and independent cities (95 counties and 38 cities that belong to no county), pre-built from TIGERweb; the instance's offline anchor layer

source.answers: Which county or independent city contains the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 133 features (95 counties and 38 independent cities, which the Census Bureau files as county equivalents), measured 2026-10-29. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: Who governs it: the board of supervisors or city council, the school board where it is elected, and a city's elected mayor, named from va-local-officials.json — the Department of Elections' results of the elections that seated them (historical.elections.virginia.gov), each member's card saying which election and linking its result. Where a body is elected by district the card names everyone and the district layers say which member represents the point. A member appointed to a vacancy is not shown until an election fills the seat, and where the results do not settle who holds a seat the card names no one and says why. Where a school board is appointed the card says so and names no one. The soil and water conservation district covering the county or city is named from the Department of Conservation and Recreation's list (dcr.virginia.gov), with the directors its voters elected from the same results, in va-conservation-boards.json; the two directors each board has appointed are not named.
source.applies: Virginia — statewide, all 95 counties and 38 independent cities.

layers.label: School Division
layers.rank_note: 135 school divisions, about 757 km2 of land on average, from TIGERweb, drawn from a mirrored tile archive; with Lexington's they cover the state exactly

source.answers: The public school division covering the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 0 (unified school districts), copied into a tile archive served from this site, re-fetched from the Census weekly; 135 features for Virginia, measured 2026-10-29.

source.people: THE CARD NAMES THE DIVISION ONLY. Its school board's members are named on the County or City card and, where they are elected by district, on the School Board District card, from the state's election results.
source.applies: Virginia — every point outside the City of Lexington. The two tilings partition the state: their Census land areas sum to exactly the 133-county-and-city total (102,256 km2), measured 2026-10-29. TIGERweb's secondary tiling is empty for Virginia (0 features).

layers.label: School Board District
layers.rank_note: 545 districts in the 98 counties and cities that elect their school board by district, each the union of its precincts in the Department of Elections' layer; 186.1 km2 mean area on the drawn file, land and water (median 158.2), measured 2026-10-30

source.answers: The district a school board member is elected from at the point, and who holds the seat. In Norfolk the point is in a ward and a superward, and the card names both.

boundary.label: Virginia Department of Elections — its statewide layer of election districts and precincts (Districts_Union_Simplified, layer 0), last changed 2026-09-22 and read 2026-10-30: 7,271 pieces joined into the 2,531 precincts they name, where two precincts claimed the same ground each part given to the precinct of the county it lies in, and checked to cover each county and city; pre-built by va/scripts/build_va_precincts.py and shipped with the app, drawn to within 12 metres. Available to anyone under § 24.2-103.1 of the Code of Virginia, as the Department told this project on 2026-10-30. A school board district is the union of the precincts the layer puts in it; in 88 counties and 10 cities the school board is elected from the same districts as the supervisors or council.

City of Norfolk — its two superwards (OpenData Maps, layer 8), from which two school board members are elected; each Norfolk precinct lies at least 99.2% inside one, so each superward is drawn as the union of its precincts.

source.people: va-local-officials.json, read from the Department of Elections' results of every local contest (historical.elections.virginia.gov) by va/scripts/build_va_local_officials.py: the winner of the latest election to each seat, the card saying which election and linking its result. A seat a special election has filled since is named from the special election. A member appointed to a vacancy is not shown until an election fills the seat, and where the results do not settle who holds a seat the card names no one and says why.
source.applies: Virginia — the 88 counties and 10 cities whose school board is elected by district. Elsewhere the board is elected at large or appointed, which the County or City card says; the layer is hidden there.

layers.label: Magisterial District
layers.rank_note: 552 records tiling the state — 513 magisterial districts, the 38 independent cities and Arlington County, which the Census files as one each — about 185 km2 of land on average, from TIGERweb, drawn from a mirrored tile archive

source.answers: The magisterial district containing the point, as the Census Bureau maps it, and its county.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 1 (county subdivisions), copied into a tile archive served from this site, re-fetched from the Census weekly; 552 features for Virginia, measured 2026-10-29: 513 magisterial districts in 94 counties, every one recorded with no government of its own; the 38 independent cities; and Arlington County, which the Census does not divide.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND THE CARD SAYS WHY. A magisterial district has no government of its own. In many counties each one elects a member of the board of supervisors, but the Census Bureau's copy can lag a county's redistricting, so this card does not use it to say who represents the point.

layers.label: Supervisor or Council District
layers.rank_note: 597 districts in the 91 counties and 15 cities that elect their board of supervisors or council by district, each the union of its precincts in the Department of Elections' layer; 176.1 km2 mean area on the drawn file, land and water (median 149.5), measured 2026-10-30

source.answers: The district a county supervisor or city council member is elected from at the point, and who holds the seat. In Norfolk the point is in a ward and a superward, and the card names both.

boundary.label: Virginia Department of Elections — its statewide layer of election districts and precincts (Districts_Union_Simplified, layer 0), last changed 2026-09-22 and read 2026-10-30: 7,271 pieces joined into the 2,531 precincts they name, where two precincts claimed the same ground each part given to the precinct of the county it lies in, and checked to cover each county and city; pre-built by va/scripts/build_va_precincts.py and shipped with the app, drawn to within 12 metres. Available to anyone under § 24.2-103.1 of the Code of Virginia, as the Department told this project on 2026-10-30. A district is the union of the precincts the layer puts in it, keyed by the layer's district number except in Southampton County (by name, its numbers being stale), Poquoson and Waynesboro (whose council districts the layer records as precincts); a district name the layer gets wrong is corrected against the name the election results give it.

City of Norfolk — its two superwards (OpenData Maps, layer 8), from which two council members are elected; each Norfolk precinct lies at least 99.2% inside one, so each superward is drawn as the union of its precincts.

source.people: va-local-officials.json, read from the Department of Elections' results of every local contest (historical.elections.virginia.gov) by va/scripts/build_va_local_officials.py: the winner of the latest election to each seat, the card saying which election and linking its result. A seat a special election has filled since is named from the special election. A member appointed to a vacancy is not shown until an election fills the seat, and where the results do not settle who holds a seat the card names no one and says why.
source.applies: Virginia — the 91 counties and 15 cities that elect their board or council by district. Arlington, Highland, Madison and Mathews counties and 23 cities elect at large; the layer is hidden there and the County or City card names the members.

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: 907 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas overlapping Virginia, of the 2,609 in the state's own bounding box, in a mirrored tile archive (measured 2026-10-29); about 94 km2 of land on average for the 2,609, and ranked by them, which are what the map draws where the archive is not used (on the raster basemap); the layer hides outside Virginia

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, copied into a tile archive served from this site, re-fetched from the Census weekly. ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='51'. 2,609 features in Virginia's box, measured 2026-10-29.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card says what the boundary actually is rather than leaving a reader to assume it means more.
source.applies: Virginia. The layer is hidden outside the state outline, because outside it the Census's point query answers with a neighbouring state's real ZIP code.

layers.label: Voting Precinct
layers.rank_note: 2,531 precincts tiling the state, pre-built from the Department of Elections' layer — 43.2 km2 mean area on the drawn file, land and water (median 7.8), measured 2026-10-30: smaller on average than a supervisor or council district, larger than a city or town (about 25 km2 of land)

source.answers: The voting precinct containing the point, and the county or city it is in.

boundary.label: Virginia Department of Elections — its statewide layer of election districts and precincts (Districts_Union_Simplified, layer 0), last changed 2026-09-22 and read 2026-10-30: 7,271 pieces joined into the 2,531 precincts they name, where two precincts claimed the same ground each part given to the precinct of the county it lies in, and checked to cover each county and city; pre-built by va/scripts/build_va_precincts.py and shipped with the app, drawn to within 12 metres. Available to anyone under § 24.2-103.1 of the Code of Virginia, as the Department told this project on 2026-10-30.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, and none is missing. A precinct elects nobody; it is where a voter's ballot is cast and counted. The card links the Department of Elections' lookup for the polling place.
source.applies: Virginia — statewide, all 133 counties and cities.

layers.label: City or Town
layers.rank_note: 227 incorporated places (38 independent cities and 189 towns), about 25 km2 of land on average, from TIGERweb, drawn from a mirrored tile archive

source.answers: The independent city or town containing the point, if any.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 4 (incorporated places), copied into a tile archive served from this site, re-fetched from the Census weekly; 227 features for Virginia (38 independent cities and 189 towns), every one recorded as an active government, measured 2026-10-29.

source.people: A city's council, elected mayor and school board are named from va-local-officials.json, the same entry its County or City card reads. Each of the 189 towns has its council and mayor named from the same results, or from the town's own page where the results do not settle the council; a council still not settled (the town elects by ward, or a special election filled a seat) names no one and says why (gap va-municipal-officeholders).
source.applies: Virginia — statewide. A point in a county outside every town is not in any city or town, which the card states.

layers.label: School Division (Elementary)
layers.rank_note: One elementary division, Lexington City Public Schools, 6.5 km2 of land, from TIGERweb, drawn from a mirrored tile archive; the ground the unified tiling leaves

source.answers: The elementary school division covering the point, where the point is in one.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 2 (elementary school districts), copied into a tile archive served from this site, re-fetched from the Census weekly; one feature for Virginia, Lexington City Public Schools, measured 2026-10-29.

source.people: THE CARD NAMES THE DIVISION ONLY. Lexington's school board is elected at large and named on the County or City card, from the state's election results.
source.applies: Virginia — the City of Lexington only. Everywhere else the School Division card is the answer.

layers.rank_note: nearest police stations by straight-line distance — a point layer, ranked with the other nearest-N layers

source.answers: The three nearest police stations to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the paged loader. Public domain. Measured 2026-10-29: 998 points in Virginia's envelope, under the service's 2,000-record cap today, and paged anyway so that stops being a fact anyone has to re-check.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a police station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: Virginia — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you. Nearest-three is a proximity fact, so for a reader near the state line the nearest one really may be in a neighbouring state, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

anchor_point.note: Virginia State Capitol, 1000 Bank Street, Richmond (an independent city)

negative_point.note: Open Atlantic Ocean east of the mouth of Chesapeake Bay, 44 km from the nearest edge of Virginia's outline — outside Virginia and outside every other instance in the fleet, and inside permalink_gate so the app answers the click and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured 2026-10-29: none of the state's shipped boundary files contains it, none of fleet-outlines.json's outlines does either, and the State Capitol, the control, is inside every shipped file. Water on purpose, the way North Carolina's and Louisiana's are: every land neighbour of Virginia is either live already (Kentucky, Tennessee, North Carolina) or a state the fleet plans to build (West Virginia, Maryland), so a point on a neighbour's land would have to move when that neighbour goes live.

geometry.note: The whole-Virginia outline for the coverage wash (loadMetroOutline), dissolved from the 133-county-and-city fabric; also the ground the ZIP layer's coverage test reads.
The 95 counties and 38 independent cities — the instance's offline anchor layer and the ground the coverage tests use.
The 11 U.S. House districts, TIGERweb layer 0 (CD120), the 2021 map, which is also layer 4's and stays in force for the 2026 election.
The 40 Virginia Senate districts, TIGERweb layer 1, the 2021 plan.
The 100 House of Delegates districts, TIGERweb layer 2, the 2021 plan.

Every Virginia voting precinct, pre-built by va/scripts/build_va_precincts.py through scripts/statewide_precincts.py from the Department of Elections' statewide layer of election districts and precincts (changed 2026-09-22, read 2026-10-30): 7,271 pieces joined into 2,531 precincts, overlaps between neighbours resolved by county, Douglas-Peucker at 12 m. 8.7 MB, 2.17 MB gzipped, fetched only when a reader switches a layer on that reads it.

The 600 supervisor, council and school board districts of the 107 counties and cities that elect by district (va/scripts/build_va_local_districts.py), each the union of its precincts in va-precincts.json; Norfolk's two superwards from the city's own map. Drawn only where va-local-officials.json names seats for the district, and the builder's --check holds the two to each other.

rosters.note: U.S. House (VA) roster, refreshed weekly by update-va-congress-roster.yml.

Virginia Senate roster from the Senate's own member list and member pages, one record per seat, refreshed weekly by update-va-legislature-roster.yml. A vacant seat carries a record saying so, so the floor is the chamber's size.
House of Delegates roster from the House's own member list and member pages, on the same terms.

Every county's board of supervisors, every city's council, every elected school board and every city's elected mayor, plus every town's council and mayor, from the Department of Elections' results (va/scripts/build_va_local_officials.py), refreshed weekly by update-va-local-officials.yml. Four top-level keys (asOf, source, localities, towns); the builder's --check holds all 133 counties and cities and every district seat.

Which of the 47 soil and water conservation districts covers each county and city, from the Department of Conservation and Recreation's list, and the directors each county's and city's voters elected, from the Department of Elections' results (va/scripts/build_va_conservation_boards.py), refreshed weekly by update-va-local-officials.yml. Four top-level keys (asOf, listRead, districts, localities); the builder's --check holds all 133 counties and cities and the seats state law gives each.
The recorded gaps this instance ships with, rendered by the data-gaps panel.
